claim: The RCK domain regulates channel gating in response to various cellular chemical stimuli in eukaryotic Slo channel families.
source: The gating ring-forming RCK domain regulates channel gating in response to various cellular chemical stimuli in eukaryotic Slo channel families and the majority of ligand-gated prokaryotic K+ channels and transporters.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general property of RCK domains.

claim: The RCK domain regulates channel gating in the majority of ligand-gated prokaryotic K+ channels and transporters.
source: The gating ring-forming RCK domain regulates channel gating in response to various cellular chemical stimuli in eukaryotic Slo channel families and the majority of ligand-gated prokaryotic K+ channels and transporters.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a general property of RCK domains.

claim: ADP activates the GsuK channel.
source: We demonstrate that ADP and NAD+ activate the GsuK channel, whereas Ca2+ serves as an allosteric inhibitor.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through functional assays and structural studies.

claim: NAD+ activates the GsuK channel.
source: We demonstrate that ADP and NAD+ activate the GsuK channel, whereas Ca2+ serves as an allosteric inhibitor.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through functional assays and structural studies.

claim: Ca2+ serves as an allosteric inhibitor of the GsuK channel.
source: We demonstrate that ADP and NAD+ activate the GsuK channel, whereas Ca2+ serves as an allosteric inhibitor.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrated through functional assays and structural studies.

claim: GsuK has a unique ion conduction pore with segmented inner helices.
source: Multiple crystal structures elucidate the structural basis of multi-ligand gating in GsuK, and also reveal a unique ion conduction pore with segmented inner helices.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: GsuK has a novel pore opening mechanics that is distinct from other K+ channels.
source: Structural comparison leads us to propose a novel pore opening mechanics that is distinct from other K+ channels.
evidence: This is proposed based on structural comparison and inference from structural data.

claim: The majority of prokaryotic ligand-gated K+ channels have one or two copies of a conserved C-terminal intracellular ligand-binding RCK domain.
source: The majority of prokaryotic ligand-gated K+ channels, as well as eukaryotic Slo channel families (Slo1 or BK, Slo2 and Slo3) (Salkoff et al., 2006), have one or two copies of a conserved C-terminal intracellular ligand-binding RCK (regulating the conductance of K+) domain (Jiang et al., 2001; Jiang et al., 2002a; Kuo et al., 2005) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Eukaryotic Slo channel families have one or two copies of a conserved C-terminal intracellular ligand-binding RCK domain.
source: The majority of prokaryotic ligand-gated K+ channels, as well as eukaryotic Slo channel families (Slo1 or BK, Slo2 and Slo3) (Salkoff et al., 2006), have one or two copies of a conserved C-terminal intracellular ligand-binding RCK (regulating the conductance of K+) domain (Jiang et al., 2001; Jiang et al., 2002a; Kuo et al., 2005) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RCK domains are ubiquitously distributed in the bacterial K+ uptake systems (Trk or Ktr systems).
source: RCK domains are also ubiquitously distributed in the bacterial K+ uptake (Trk or Ktr systems) (Schlösser et al., 1993; Nakamura et al., 1998) and efflux machinery (Kef systems) (Bakker et al., 1987; Munro et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: RCK domains are ubiquitously distributed in the bacterial K+ efflux machinery (Kef systems).
source: RCK domains are also ubiquitously distributed in the bacterial K+ uptake (Trk or Ktr systems) (Schlösser et al., 1993; Nakamura et al., 1998) and efflux machinery (Kef systems) (Bakker et al., 1987; Munro et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The wide distribution of RCK domains in K+ channels and transporters highlights their importance in regulating K+ transport across the cell membrane.
source: The wide distribution of RCK domains in K+ channels and transporters highlights their importance in regulating K+ transport across the cell membrane.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed distribution of RCK domains.

claim: RCK domains associate as a dimer.
source: RCK domains associate as a dimer, (Jiang et al., 2001; Roosild et al., 2002; Dong et al., 2005), which serves as the basic building block for the quaternary structural assembly in both K+ channels and transporters.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The RCK dimer serves as the basic building block for the quaternary structural assembly in both K+ channels and transporters.
source: RCK domains associate as a dimer, (Jiang et al., 2001; Roosild et al., 2002; Dong et al., 2005), which serves as the basic building block for the quaternary structural assembly in both K+ channels and transporters.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Four RCK dimers assemble into an octameric gating ring in a functional MthK channel tetramer.
source: As demonstrated in the structure of MthK, a Ca2+-gated K+ channel from Methanobacterium thermoautotrophicum, four RCK dimers assemble into an octameric gating ring in a functional channel tetramer (Jiang et al., 2002a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to the MthK structure.

claim: A gating ring of eight RCK domains is the functional assembly for both K+ channels and transporters.
source: The same quaternary complex is also observed in the K+ transporter systems (Albright et al., 2006), indicating that a gating ring of eight RCK domains is the functional assembly for both channels and transporters.
evidence: This is supported by citation and inference from structural observations.

claim: Most prokaryotic RCK-containing K+ channels have only one copy of the RCK domain on each subunit.
source: Most prokaryotic RCK-containing K+ channels have only one copy of the RCK domain on each subunit and the formation of an octameric gating ring requires the co-expression of their cytosolic RCK domain via an alternative internal translation start site on the same gene (Jiang et al., 2002a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The formation of an octameric gating ring in most prokaryotic RCK-containing K+ channels requires the co-expression of their cytosolic RCK domain via an alternative internal translation start site on the same gene.
source: Most prokaryotic RCK-containing K+ channels have only one copy of the RCK domain on each subunit and the formation of an octameric gating ring requires the co-expression of their cytosolic RCK domain via an alternative internal translation start site on the same gene (Jiang et al., 2002a).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Eukaryotic Slo K+ channel families contain two tandem RCK domains on each subunit.
source: The eukaryotic Slo K+ channel families and a subset of prokaryotic K+ channels already contain two tandem RCK domains on each subunit and therefore the gating ring assembly in these channels no longer requires the co-expression of an isolated RCK domain (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated as a structural feature of Slo channels.

claim: A subset of prokaryotic K+ channels contain two tandem RCK domains on each subunit.
source: The eukaryotic Slo K+ channel families and a subset of prokaryotic K+ channels already contain two tandem RCK domains on each subunit and therefore the gating ring assembly in these channels no longer requires the co-expression of an isolated RCK domain (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is stated as a structural feature of certain prokaryotic channels.

claim: The gating ring assembly in channels with two tandem RCK domains does not require the co-expression of an isolated RCK domain.
source: The eukaryotic Slo K+ channel families and a subset of prokaryotic K+ channels already contain two tandem RCK domains on each subunit and therefore the gating ring assembly in these channels no longer requires the co-expression of an isolated RCK domain (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural organization of these channels.

claim: The formation of the gating ring provides a platform for diverse allosteric ligand regulation among RCK-containing channels.
source: The formation of the gating ring provides a platform for diverse allosteric ligand regulation among RCK-containing channels, and the gating rings of some channels are susceptible to multiple cellular stimuli.
evidence: This is an inference based on the structural and functional properties of gating rings.

claim: The gating rings of some RCK-containing channels are susceptible to multiple cellular stimuli.
source: The formation of the gating ring provides a platform for diverse allosteric ligand regulation among RCK-containing channels, and the gating rings of some channels are susceptible to multiple cellular stimuli.
evidence: This is supported by the example of BK channels.

claim: The RCK domains of BK channels have multiple divalent cation (Ca2+ and Mg2+) binding sites for channel activation.
source: For example, the RCK domains of BK channels have multiple divalent cation (Ca2+ and Mg2+) binding sites for channel activation and can be modulated by phosphorylation and heme binding, and so on (Zhang et al., 2001; Shi et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002; Bao et al., 2004; Zeng et al., 2005; Hou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BK channels can be modulated by phosphorylation.
source: For example, the RCK domains of BK channels have multiple divalent cation (Ca2+ and Mg2+) binding sites for channel activation and can be modulated by phosphorylation and heme binding, and so on (Zhang et al., 2001; Shi et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002; Bao et al., 2004; Zeng et al., 2005; Hou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: BK channels can be modulated by heme binding.
source: For example, the RCK domains of BK channels have multiple divalent cation (Ca2+ and Mg2+) binding sites for channel activation and can be modulated by phosphorylation and heme binding, and so on (Zhang et al., 2001; Shi et al., 2002; Xia et al., 2002; Bao et al., 2004; Zeng et al., 2005; Hou et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The structural information of RCK-containing channels has been limited to the low resolution single-RCK MthK channel in a Ca2+-bound, open conformation.
source: The structural information of RCK-containing channels has been limited to the low resolution single-RCK MthK channel in a Ca2+-bound, open conformation (Jiang et al., 2002a) or the isolated cytosolic RCK domains from other K+ channels and transporters (Roosild et al., 2002; Albright et al., 2006; Ye et al., 2006; Wu et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2010; Yuan et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: The ion conduction pore of MthK was poorly defined due to resolution limit and poor crystal packing.
source: Due to the resolution limit and poor crystal packing, the ion conduction pore of MthK was poorly defined and the linkers between the pore and the gating ring, which are essential for coupling the gating ring conformational change to the pore opening and closing, could not be resolved in the structure.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the MthK structure.

claim: The linkers between the pore and the gating ring in MthK could not be resolved in the structure.
source: Due to the resolution limit and poor crystal packing, the ion conduction pore of MthK was poorly defined and the linkers between the pore and the gating ring, which are essential for coupling the gating ring conformational change to the pore opening and closing, could not be resolved in the structure.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the MthK structure.

claim: The linkers between the pore and the gating ring are essential for coupling the gating ring conformational change to the pore opening and closing.
source: Due to the resolution limit and poor crystal packing, the ion conduction pore of MthK was poorly defined and the linkers between the pore and the gating ring, which are essential for coupling the gating ring conformational change to the pore opening and closing, could not be resolved in the structure.
evidence: This is an inference based on the functional role of linkers.

claim: GsuK is a two-transmembrane, RCK-regulated K+ channel.
source: In this study, we present structural and functional studies of a novel a two-transmembrane, RCK-regulated K+ channel, GsuK, named after the bacterium Geobacter sulfurreducens from which this K+ channel was cloned.
evidence: This is a structural characterization of GsuK.

claim: GsuK was cloned from the bacterium Geobacter sulfurreducens.
source: In this study, we present structural and functional studies of a novel a two-transmembrane, RCK-regulated K+ channel, GsuK, named after the bacterium Geobacter sulfurreducens from which this K+ channel was cloned.
evidence: This is stated as the source of the channel.

claim: Each GsuK subunit contains two tandem RCK domains.
source: Each GsuK subunit contains two tandem RCK domains, reminiscent of Slo K+ channels.
evidence: This is a structural characterization of GsuK.

claim: GsuK is a nucleotide-activated K+ channel.
source: We demonstrate that GsuK is a nucleotide-activated and Ca2+-deactivated K+ channel and reveal the structural mechanism of multi-ligand gating of this double-RCK K+ channel and a distinct pore opening mechanics.
evidence: This is a primary finding from functional assays.

claim: GsuK is a Ca2+-deactivated K+ channel.
source: We demonstrate that GsuK is a nucleotide-activated and Ca2+-deactivated K+ channel and reveal the structural mechanism of multi-ligand gating of this double-RCK K+ channel and a distinct pore opening mechanics.
evidence: This is a primary finding from functional assays.

claim: The two intracellular ligand binding RCK domains of GsuK form a bi-lobed structure equivalent to the MthK RCK dimer.
source: The two intracellular ligand binding RCK domains form a bi-lobed structure equivalent to the MthK RCK dimer; each lobe consists of the N-terminal two-thirds of the RCK domain (βA to αF) and adopts a Rossmann-fold (Rossmann et al., 1974) (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: Each lobe of the GsuK RCK domain consists of the N-terminal two-thirds of the RCK domain (βA to αF) and adopts a Rossmann-fold.
source: The two intracellular ligand binding RCK domains form a bi-lobed structure equivalent to the MthK RCK dimer; each lobe consists of the N-terminal two-thirds of the RCK domain (βA to αF) and adopts a Rossmann-fold (Rossmann et al., 1974) (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The secondary structural elements of the C-terminal subdomains are similar between GsuK and MthK.
source: While the secondary structural elements of the C-terminal subdomains are similar between GsuK and MthK, their tertiary structural arrangements are quite distinct.
evidence: This is a structural comparison between GsuK and MthK.

claim: The tertiary structural arrangements of the C-terminal subdomains are quite distinct between GsuK and MthK.
source: While the secondary structural elements of the C-terminal subdomains are similar between GsuK and MthK, their tertiary structural arrangements are quite distinct.
evidence: This is a structural comparison between GsuK and MthK.

claim: In MthK, the N-terminal lobes and the C-terminal subdomains of the RCK dimer are connected by interlocking helix-turn-helix motifs (αF-turn-αG).
source: In MthK, the N-terminal lobes and the C-terminal subdomains of the RCK dimer are connected by interlocking helix-turn-helix motifs (αF-turn-αG), which provide extensive dimerization interactions at the so-called flexible interface (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a structural description of MthK.

claim: The interlocking helix-turn-helix motifs in MthK provide extensive dimerization interactions at the flexible interface.
source: In MthK, the N-terminal lobes and the C-terminal subdomains of the RCK dimer are connected by interlocking helix-turn-helix motifs (αF-turn-αG), which provide extensive dimerization interactions at the so-called flexible interface (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a structural description of MthK.

claim: In GsuK, the equivalent αG helix is absent in RCK1.
source: In GsuK, the equivalent αG helix is absent in RCK1 and becomes a shorter helix with a different orientation in RCK2, resulting in swapped and loosely packed C-terminal subdomains (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: In GsuK, the equivalent αG helix becomes a shorter helix with a different orientation in RCK2.
source: In GsuK, the equivalent αG helix is absent in RCK1 and becomes a shorter helix with a different orientation in RCK2, resulting in swapped and loosely packed C-terminal subdomains (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The absence and modification of the αG helix in GsuK results in swapped and loosely packed C-terminal subdomains.
source: In GsuK, the equivalent αG helix is absent in RCK1 and becomes a shorter helix with a different orientation in RCK2, resulting in swapped and loosely packed C-terminal subdomains (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: Four GsuK intracellular subunits assemble into a gating ring containing eight RCK domains through inter-subunit interactions at the assembly interfaces.
source: Four GsuK intracellular subunits assemble into a gating ring containing eight RCK domains through inter-subunit interactions at the assembly interfaces (Figure 4A,B), with the N-terminal Rossmann-folded lobe of each RCK forming the core of the gating ring and the C-terminal subdomain loosely associating with the core of the gating ring on the periphery.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The N-terminal Rossmann-folded lobe of each RCK forms the core of the GsuK gating ring.
source: Four GsuK intracellular subunits assemble into a gating ring containing eight RCK domains through inter-subunit interactions at the assembly interfaces (Figure 4A,B), with the N-terminal Rossmann-folded lobe of each RCK forming the core of the gating ring and the C-terminal subdomain loosely associating with the core of the gating ring on the periphery.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The C-terminal subdomain of each RCK loosely associates with the core of the GsuK gating ring on the periphery.
source: Four GsuK intracellular subunits assemble into a gating ring containing eight RCK domains through inter-subunit interactions at the assembly interfaces (Figure 4A,B), with the N-terminal Rossmann-folded lobe of each RCK forming the core of the gating ring and the C-terminal subdomain loosely associating with the core of the gating ring on the periphery.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The GsuK gating ring is not twofold symmetrical because it is formed by two different sets of RCK domains.
source: As the GsuK gating ring is formed by two different sets of RCK domains, its top and bottom halves are not twofold symmetrical, as seen in the MthK gating ring.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: The pore-connecting top half of the GsuK gating ring is in a contracted form similar to the closed MthK.
source: The pore-connecting top half of the GsuK gating ring is in a contracted form similar to the closed MthK whereas the bottom half is more expanded (Figure 4C), suggesting that the structure likely represents a closed conformation.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The bottom half of the GsuK gating ring is more expanded than the top half.
source: The pore-connecting top half of the GsuK gating ring is in a contracted form similar to the closed MthK whereas the bottom half is more expanded (Figure 4C), suggesting that the structure likely represents a closed conformation.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The GsuK gating ring structure likely represents a closed conformation.
source: The pore-connecting top half of the GsuK gating ring is in a contracted form similar to the closed MthK whereas the bottom half is more expanded (Figure 4C), suggesting that the structure likely represents a closed conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural comparison with MthK.

claim: Each GsuK subunit contains a small fragment of the pore-lining inner helix at its N-terminus, which forms a short four-helix bundle atop the center of the gating ring.
source: Furthermore, each subunit also contains a small fragment of the pore-lining inner helix at its N-terminus, which forms a short four-helix bundle atop the center of the gating ring and creates a constriction point at the intracellular end of the pore that would occlude the passage of hydrated K+ ions (Figure 4A,D).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The four-helix bundle in GsuK creates a constriction point at the intracellular end of the pore that would occlude the passage of hydrated K+ ions.
source: Furthermore, each subunit also contains a small fragment of the pore-lining inner helix at its N-terminus, which forms a short four-helix bundle atop the center of the gating ring and creates a constriction point at the intracellular end of the pore that would occlude the passage of hydrated K+ ions (Figure 4A,D).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: The same closed gate is observed in the structures of the full-length GsuK channel.
source: The same closed gate is also observed in the structures of the full-length channel as discussed later.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The helix bundle in GsuK is tethered to RCK1 by linkers in an extended configuration.
source: The helix bundle is tethered to RCK1 by linkers in an extended configuration, ensuring a tight coupling between the gating ring conformational change and pore opening at the intracellular gate (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The extended linker configuration in GsuK ensures a tight coupling between the gating ring conformational change and pore opening at the intracellular gate.
source: The helix bundle is tethered to RCK1 by linkers in an extended configuration, ensuring a tight coupling between the gating ring conformational change and pore opening at the intracellular gate (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is an inference based on structural observations.

claim: The position and structural features of the linker in GsuK are similar to that observed in the BK channel gating ring.
source: Despite low sequence similarity, the position and structural features of this linker are similar to that observed in the BK channel gating ring (Wu et al., 2010) (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a structural comparison supported by citation.

claim: The RCK2 domain of GsuK contains the conserved GxGxxG…D/E sequence motif for nucleotide binding in Rossmann-folded protein.
source: The RCK2 domain of GsuK contains the conserved GxGxxG…D/E sequence motif for nucleotide binding in Rossmann-folded protein (Bellamacina, 1996) (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a sequence analysis supported by citation.

claim: Electron density modeled as AMP was observed at the predicted nucleotide binding site in the GsuK gating ring structure.
source: Indeed, electron density modeled as AMP was observed at the predicted nucleotide binding site in the GsuK gating ring structure (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: No nucleotides were added during protein purification or crystallization of the GsuK gating ring.
source: As no nucleotides were added during protein purification or crystallization, the bound nucleotide is likely from the E. coli cells used for protein expression.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental procedure.

claim: The bound nucleotide in the GsuK gating ring structure is likely from the E. coli cells used for protein expression.
source: As no nucleotides were added during protein purification or crystallization, the bound nucleotide is likely from the E. coli cells used for protein expression.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental procedure.

claim: The electron density in the GsuK gating ring structure could be from other adenine-containing nucleotide whose AMP moiety is well structured while the rest is mobile.
source: Although modeled as AMP, the electron density could actually be from other adenine-containing nucleotide whose AMP moiety is well structured while the rest is mobile.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural observations.

claim: In the structure of the nucleotide binding RCK domain from a K+ transporter, only the AMP portion of a bound NAD+ can be defined.
source: This is the case in the structure of the nucleotide binding RCK domain from a K+ transporter, in which only the AMP portion of a bound NAD+ can be defined (Roosild et al., 2002; Albright et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural studies.

claim: ADP and NAD+ are the likely ligands for GsuK.
source: Supporting this hypothesis, our functional characterization using the 86Rb flux assay demonstrated that ADP and NAD+ are the likely ligands for GsuK as discussed below.
evidence: This is supported by functional assay data.

claim: Two bound metal ions were observed in each GsuK subunit.
source: Two bound metal ions were observed in each GsuK subunit.
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: One metal ion in GsuK is identified as Zn2+ as it is chelated by His (His359 and His391) and Cys, (Cys364 and Cys388) in RCK2.
source: One is identified as Zn2+ as it is chelated by His (His359 and His391) and Cys, (Cys364 and Cys388) in RCK2 (Figure 5B) with ion coordination chemistry and the local structure resembling a zinc-finger motif; fluorescence scanning of the crystal at the synchrotron also confirmed the presence of Zn2+ in the crystal.
evidence: This is a structural finding confirmed by fluorescence scanning.

claim: Fluorescence scanning of the GsuK crystal at the synchrotron confirmed the presence of Zn2+ in the crystal.
source: One is identified as Zn2+ as it is chelated by His (His359 and His391) and Cys, (Cys364 and Cys388) in RCK2 (Figure 5B) with ion coordination chemistry and the local structure resembling a zinc-finger motif; fluorescence scanning of the crystal at the synchrotron also confirmed the presence of Zn2+ in the crystal.
evidence: This is experimental data from fluorescence scanning.

claim: Whether Zn2+ plays any functional role in GsuK is still unclear and warrants further study.
source: Whether Zn2+ plays any functional role is still unclear and warrants further study.
evidence: This is a statement about the uncertainty of Zn2+ function.

claim: The second bound ion in GsuK is identified as Ca2+ based on ligand chemistry and functional assays.
source: The second bound ion, identified as Ca2+ based on ligand chemistry and functional assays, is positioned at the inter-subunit assembly interface, a location reminiscent of the Ca2+ bowl in BK channel (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a structural finding supported by functional assays.

claim: The Ca2+ binding site in GsuK is positioned at the inter-subunit assembly interface.
source: The second bound ion, identified as Ca2+ based on ligand chemistry and functional assays, is positioned at the inter-subunit assembly interface, a location reminiscent of the Ca2+ bowl in BK channel (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: The Ca2+ binding site in GsuK is reminiscent of the Ca2+ bowl in BK channel.
source: The second bound ion, identified as Ca2+ based on ligand chemistry and functional assays, is positioned at the inter-subunit assembly interface, a location reminiscent of the Ca2+ bowl in BK channel (Figure 5C,D).
evidence: This is a structural comparison.

claim: The six oxygen ligands for Ca2+ in GsuK come from Thr183, Asn210 and Thr214 of RCK1 and Glu449, Asn450 and Gln453 of RCK2 from the neighboring subunit.
source: The six oxygen ligands, two of which are backbone carbonyl oxygen atoms, come from Thr183, Asn210 and Thr214 of RCK1 and Glu449, Asn450 and Gln453 of RCK2 from the neighboring subunit (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: Two of the six oxygen ligands for Ca2+ in GsuK are backbone carbonyl oxygen atoms.
source: The six oxygen ligands, two of which are backbone carbonyl oxygen atoms, come from Thr183, Asn210 and Thr214 of RCK1 and Glu449, Asn450 and Gln453 of RCK2 from the neighboring subunit (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a structural finding from crystal structures.

claim: Ca2+ serves as an allosteric inhibitor in GsuK whose binding stabilizes the closed gating ring and deactivates the channel.
source: Unlike that in MthK or BK, Ca2+ serves as an allosteric inhibitor in GsuK whose binding stabilizes the closed gating ring and deactivates the channel as confirmed by single channel electrophysiology and the full-length channel structure.
evidence: This is supported by functional assays and structural data.

claim: The crystallization conditions for the GsuK gating ring contain neither Zn2+ nor Ca2+.
source: As the crystallization conditions contain neither Zn2+ nor Ca2+, both ions are likely from the E. coli cells or trace amounts of contaminants in the solutions used for protein purification and crystallization.
evidence: This is a statement about the experimental procedure.

claim: Both Zn2+ and Ca2+ in the GsuK gating ring structure are likely from the E. coli cells or trace amounts of contaminants in the solutions used for protein purification and crystallization.
source: As the crystallization conditions contain neither Zn2+ nor Ca2+, both ions are likely from the E. coli cells or trace amounts of contaminants in the solutions used for protein purification and crystallization.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental procedure.

claim: Among nucleotides tested, guanidine nucleotides had no effect on 86Rb influx into GsuK-containing liposomes as compared to the control liposomes absent of nucleotide.
source: Among those nucleotides tested, guanidine nucleotides had no effect on 86Rb influx as compared to the control liposomes absent of nucleotide, while ADP and NAD+ led to about a 4–5-fold increase in intraliposomal radioactivity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is data from the 86Rb flux assay.

claim: ADP led to about a 4–5-fold increase in intraliposomal radioactivity in the 86Rb flux assay.
source: Among those nucleotides tested, guanidine nucleotides had no effect on 86Rb influx as compared to the control liposomes absent of nucleotide, while ADP and NAD+ led to about a 4–5-fold increase in intraliposomal radioactivity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is data from the 86Rb flux assay.

claim: NAD+ led to about a 4–5-fold increase in intraliposomal radioactivity in the 86Rb flux assay.
source: Among those nucleotides tested, guanidine nucleotides had no effect on 86Rb influx as compared to the control liposomes absent of nucleotide, while ADP and NAD+ led to about a 4–5-fold increase in intraliposomal radioactivity (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is data from the 86Rb flux assay.

claim: Other adenine-containing nucleotides such as ATP, AMP, or NADH had no obvious effect on 86Rb influx in the flux assay.
source: Interestingly, other adenine-containing nucleotides such as ATP, AMP, or NADH had no obvious effect on 86Rb influx.
evidence: This is data from the 86Rb flux assay.

claim: In the absence of intracellular Ca2+, both the wild-type GsuK and L97D mutant channels exhibit high single channel activity with an open probability (Po) of about 0.9.
source: In the absence of intracellular Ca2+, both the wild-type and mutant channels exhibit high single channel activity with an open probability (Po) of about 0.9 (Figure 6B–D).
evidence: This is data from single channel recordings.

claim: The L97D mutation resulted in a significantly higher single channel conductance than the wild-type GsuK channel.
source: The L97D mutation resulted in a significantly higher single channel conductance than the wild-type channel.
evidence: This is data from single channel recordings.

claim: Both wild-type GsuK and L97D mutant channels are weakly K+ selective, with a reversal potential of about −40 mV under bi-ionic conditions.
source: Both channels are weakly K+ selective, with a reversal potential of about −40 mV under bi-ionic conditions, equivalent to a permeability ratio (PNa/PK) of about 0.2 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is data from single channel recordings.

claim: The permeability ratio (PNa/PK) of GsuK is about 0.2.
source: Both channels are weakly K+ selective, with a reversal potential of about −40 mV under bi-ionic conditions, equivalent to a permeability ratio (PNa/PK) of about 0.2 (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is data from single channel recordings.

claim: The weak K+ selectivity of GsuK could be partly attributed to the presence of Phe instead of Tyr in the selectivity filter.
source: The weak K+ selectivity could be partly attributed to the presence of Phe instead of Tyr in the selectivity filter as demonstrated in a recent selectivity study on K+ channel in which replacing Tyr with Phe in the filter results in a decreased K+ selectivity (Sauer et al., 2011).

claim: The presence of lipids may be necessary to stabilize the GsuK pore in an open state and give rise to a lower efficacy of Ca2+ deactivation.
source: As lipids are known to be important for membrane protein stability, their presence may be necessary to stabilize the GsuK pore in an open state and, therefore, give rise to a lower efficacy of Ca2+ deactivation.
evidence: This is speculation based on the role of lipids.

claim: A possible region in GsuK for lipid interactions is the stretch of positively charged residues surrounding the closed gate at the carboxyl terminus of the inner helix.
source: A possible region in GsuK for lipid interactions is the stretch of positively charged residues surrounding the closed gate at the carboxyl terminus of the inner helix, which could potentially interact with the phospholipid head groups and influence channel gating.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural observations.

claim: The positively charged residues at the carboxyl terminus of the inner helix could potentially interact with the phospholipid head groups and influence channel gating.

claim: The majority of Slo2.1 and Slo3 channels have the same TVGFG signature sequence as GsuK.
source: Like GsuK, the majority of Slo2.1 and Slo3 channels have the same TVGFG signature sequence, and a study of mouse Slo3 showed a K+ selectivity similar to that of GsuK (Schreiber et al., 1998).
evidence: This is a sequence comparison supported by citation.

claim: The Slo2 inner helix contains a conserved Pro at the position equivalent to the helix breaking Leu97 of GsuK, suggesting a similar inner helix break.
source: The Slo2 inner helix contains a conserved Pro at the position equivalent to the helix breaking Leu97 of GsuK, suggesting a similar inner helix break.

claim: NAD+ has been shown to modulate Na+ activation in Slo2 by binding at the same nucleotide site in RCK2.
source: NAD+ has also been shown in a recent study to modulate Na+ activation in Slo2 by binding at the same nucleotide site in RCK2 (Tamsett et al., 2009).

claim: The relative orientation between the transmembrane pore and the gating ring in Slo channels may have a closer resemblance to GsuK than MthK.
source: Furthermore, the relative orientation between the transmembrane pore and the gating ring in Slo channels, and consequently pore opening mechanism, may have a closer resemblance to GsuK than MthK.
evidence: This is speculation based on structural comparison.

claim: The acidic Asp90 residue in the S0–S1 loop of the BK channel transmembrane pore has been shown to interact with the Glu374/Glu399 Mg2+ site from the neighboring subunits.
source: One piece of evidence is that the acidic Asp90 residue in the S0–S1 loop of the BK channel transmembrane pore has been shown to interact with the Glu374/Glu399 Mg2+ site from the neighboring subunits (Yang et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Docking of the Kv channel pore onto the BK gating ring using MthK as a model would position the Asp90-Glu374/Glu399 interaction within the same subunit.
source: Docking of the Kv channel pore onto the BK gating ring using MthK as a model would position such interaction within the same subunit (Wu et al., 2010), but is otherwise possible if using GsuK as a structural model.
evidence: This is an inference based on structural modeling supported by citation.
